commit: 79837f3 (round 1, incomplete) + ce13a5b (round 2, landed) fix(menubar): re-anchor attention bubble during drag
problem: Dragging the floating pet (Maew) while an attention bubble is displayed detaches the bubble: it stays pinned at its old anchor instead of tracking the pet during the drag.
solution: Round 1 (79837f3, INCOMPLETE) re-anchored the bubble via frameChangeHandler — but that handler fires only on mouseUp, because state persistence is deliberately deferred off the per-tick drag path for perf (phase-04). So the bubble only snapped back at drag END. Round 2 (ce13a5b, LANDED) adds a separate liveFrameChangeHandler fired from applyPanelFrame on every mouseDragged/resize tick doing a cheap in-memory bubble re-anchor; persistence stays on mouseUp. Do not collapse the two handlers back into one — the live (per-tick, no I/O) and committed (mouseUp, persists) paths have different cost budgets.
prompt_lesson: Two transferable lessons. (1) For any draggable/resizable container, enumerate every child or attached overlay (bubbles, badges, affordances, pills) and assert each tracks the same transform — coordinate-space cohesion is the UI analogue of cross-file-atomicity. (2) The round-1 miss is its own class: chrome re-anchoring must hook the LIVE per-tick move path, not a persisted-on-mouseUp handler. A perf optimization that defers state writes off the drag hot path will silently starve any overlay that piggybacks on the persist callback. When you see a deferred/debounced commit path, ask what else needed the high-frequency signal it dropped. Reachability caveat: only review-reachable when container drag-handler + overlay live in the same ticket diff; here pet (P4) and bubble (P6) shipped in different phases, so per-ticket review saw neither pair — integration-of-features bugs need a phase-level review pass.
test_reachability: Weak. Integration behavior: a real NSPanel drag emitting per-tick frame moves while an AttentionBubblePanel is live. BubbleLayout.frame is a pure function and was already correct; the regression was the missing *call* on the live drag path. FloatingPetPanelSpy (controller tests) does not exercise it. Verified by build + manual drag QA across both rounds — round 1 passed build but failed manual QA, which is exactly why ledger lines are written at verified-commit time, not on first green build.
rounds_note: Round 1 was committed+recorded prematurely (as rounds:1) before human verification and proved incomplete. Folded into one entry rather than codogotchi-02 — same bug, same gap. Methodology takeaway: when a fix does not one-shot, instrument critical paths with debug logging to find the real signal flow before guessing again (here: logging would have shown frameChangeHandler firing only on mouseUp).

problem: The Focus button in the attention bubble (1) always focused a hardcoded IDE app regardless of where the hook actually fired from, and (2) could not distinguish between VS Code forks (Cursor, Insiders, Antigravity) or reach Zed/VS Code Insiders/Antigravity embedded terminals at all. Standalone terminals (Warp, Ghostty, Terminal.app) were unreachable. Codex Desktop was misidentified as claude_code due to PascalCase event name collision.
solution: Four-layer fix: (1) CODOGOTCHI_ORIGIN=codex env var injected into Codex Desktop hook command to override PascalCase heuristic; (2) detectTerminalBundleId() in hook-binary.ts detects parent terminal from well-known env vars and writes terminal_bundle_id into source_event in state.json; (3) __CFBundleIdentifier fallback catches any IDE that directly spawns a shell without login intermediary — confirmed working for VS Code Insiders, Antigravity, Zed; (4) Focus button priority: terminal_bundle_id first → IDE-native origin map (cursor, codex) → no-op. Round 1 shipped correct architecture but missed IDE embedded terminals. Round 2 added Zed (ZED_TERM), __CFBundleIdentifier VS Code fork disambiguation, and __CFBundleIdentifier catch-all. Debug dump (CODOGOTCHI_DEBUG_TERMINAL=1 codogotchi-hook) used to validate each terminal, then stripped.
prompt_lesson: The Focus button was specified against a fixed origin→app map. No ticket asked 'what app should Focus target when origin=claude_code running in a terminal?' — the spec assumed a 1:1 mapping that doesn't exist for CLI tools. Lesson: for any user-facing action that targets an external app, the spec must enumerate the CLI-vs-IDE distinction and the embedded-terminal case explicitly. A reviewer reading the phase-06 tickets had no way to flag this because the gap was in the requirements, not the implementation.
test_reachability: None — terminal detection requires real process spawn chains. Unit-testable in isolation (detectTerminalBundleId is a pure function of env), but the end-to-end path (IDE spawns shell → hook fires → state.json written → bubble reads it → Focus tapped) is integration-only. The pure function is exported and testable; integration is verified by CODOGOTCHI_DEBUG_TERMINAL=1 spot-checks.

commit: 000375f feat(soa): append gate transition telemetry log
problem: The direct SoA gate sidecar only preserved the resident last-write-wins `gate.json` payload. Once a ticket moved through multiple gates, there was no durable record of which gates fired for that ticket or what `{ since, expires_at }` window was emitted for each one, which blocked empirical TTL tuning and post-hoc inspection.
solution: Keep `gate.json` as the renderer input, but append every emitted gate payload to `$CODOGOTCHI_HOME/gate-transitions.log` as one JSON line with the same `{ gate, since, expires_at, plan_key, ticket_id }` shape. This preserves transition order and the exact TTL window written for each emission without changing render behavior. Do not try to reconstruct history from resident `gate.json`; the append-only log is the audit trail.
prompt_lesson: When a feature intentionally uses an ephemeral last-write-wins sidecar for live behavior, ask separately whether operators also need a history lane for tuning and diagnosis. Current-state transport and observability history are different products.
test_reachability: Good. Cheap automated coverage can assert that every `writeGateEvent` call appends one line to `gate-transitions.log`, and multi-transition flows can assert ordering (`ticket_completed` before `ticket_started` in cook-mode advance). End-to-end behavior was also verified by simulating a full ticket gate sequence and by empirical confirmation that TTL still limits rendered gate lifetimes correctly.

commit: 983bd28 fix(menubar): scale gate badges with floating pet
problem: The floating SoA gate badges stayed at a fixed visual size while the floating pet itself resized, so shrinking or enlarging the pet broke the chrome-to-pet proportion and made the badges look detached from the transformed frame.
solution: Derive gate badge metrics from the floating pet frame width instead of hardcoding them. Padding, badge height, corner radius, inter-badge spacing, and font size now scale with the pet width and clamp to a minimum so tiny pets do not collapse. The badge panel continues to remeasure during reposition, so drag/resize keeps the scaled chrome anchored correctly.
prompt_lesson: When a ticket adds chrome attached to a resizable surface, the spec must say whether that chrome is fixed-size or scales with the host. Anchoring alone is not enough; transform behavior is a separate requirement that should be spelled out and reviewed explicitly.
test_reachability: Good for automated layout math, limited for final aesthetics. Pure tests can assert that larger pet widths produce larger badge metrics and that very small widths clamp at a minimum scale, which now exists in controller coverage. Final acceptance still benefits from visual QA because proportional correctness is partly perceptual.

commit: ae4da1b feat(menubar): log tool_command and reason_kind in transition log + cad7526 fix(hook): classify ci scripts as testing
problem: state.json already carried tool_command (the raw Bash/Shell command the producer classified) and attention.reason_kind, but state-transitions.log recorded only ts/state/prev/source_origin/source_kind/source_name. state.json is a single last-write-wins snapshot overwritten on every event, so the only durable, append-only record was missing exactly the fields needed to audit producer-side behavior after the fact. This was caught by spotting live in state.json that `bun run ci` was being bucketed as the generic `implementing` fallback instead of `testing` — a misclassification that would have been invisible from the durable log because the command that drove a transition was never recorded. The reason_kind gap is the same shape: standby and errored both gate the attention bubble but the log could not say which attention path fired.
solution: Add tool_command and reason_kind to the transition-log NDJSON line. Decode tool_command in StateJsonReader (reason_kind was already decoded into AttentionPayload.reasonKind), thread both through StateSnapshot, and emit them in TransitionLog.LinePayload via encodeIfPresent so they are omitted on non-shell transitions and heartbeats. The linked-but-separate heuristic defect (`bun run ci` and siblings missing from TEST_RUNNER_PREFIXES) was patched directly in the same pass: ci-family scripts now classify as testing; the word-boundary matcher treats `:` as a stop so ci:quiet needs its own prefix entry.
prompt_lesson: When a producer enriches a live last-write-wins snapshot with new diagnostic fields (here tool_command and attention.reason_kind), the matching append-only audit log must be updated in lockstep or the enrichment is only observable by watching the snapshot at the right millisecond. Current-state transport and observability history are different products and drift apart silently. A second lesson surfaced from the same gap: heuristic classifiers (TEST_RUNNER_PREFIXES) are only auditable retroactively if the input that drove each classification is itself logged — otherwise misroutes like `bun run ci`->implementing are pure luck to catch.
test_reachability: Good. TransitionLogTests now asserts both fields appear when present and are omitted when absent; the existing source-field-omission test covers the lean-line contract. hook-binary tests cover the ci-family classification. Known coverage limit (documented, not yet closed): transition lines fire only on state change, so a command that does not change state is still not logged at all — full command-level auditing would need per-event logging, deliberately deferred for volume/rotation cost.

commit: aa0ac3a fix(test): stop router-help-trim setup test from clobbering real IDE config
problem: Codex Desktop telemetry silently vanished from ~/.codogotchi/state-transitions.log after 2026-05-31T16:26:03Z (no codex-origin lines thereafter), while claude_code lines continued. Initial hypothesis was that Codex was bridging to the claude_code origin via the PascalCase heuristic. That was wrong: CODOGOTCHI_ORIGIN=codex was still correctly set in ~/.codex/hooks.json. The real cause: the bare-dispatch reachability tests in router-help-trim.test.ts set CODOGOTCHI_HOME to /tmp/nonexistent-${Date.now()} but did NOT set CODOGOTCHI_USER_ROOT. installHooks resolves IDE-config paths via getUserRoot() (CODOGOTCHI_USER_ROOT or homedir()), NOT CODOGOTCHI_HOME, so on a fresh sandbox home `setup` ran to completion and rewrote the developer's REAL ~/.codex/hooks.json and ~/.codex/hooks/codogotchi.toml, baking CODOGOTCHI_HOME=/tmp/nonexistent into the hook command. Codex then wrote its state to a throwaway /tmp dir that never existed for the renderer. Every `bun test`/`bun run ci` re-corrupted it — and because the SoA review subagent for phase 08 was run via codex-cli, running the suite broke Codex's own hooks (a self-inflicted feedback loop). ~/.cursor/hooks.json and ~/.claude/settings.json were untouched (Cursor uses a separate installer the bare setup did not trigger; Claude hooks omit CODOGOTCHI_HOME entirely).
solution: Sandbox BOTH CODOGOTCHI_HOME and CODOGOTCHI_USER_ROOT to fresh temp dirs in the offending tests, and seed config.json in the home so `setup` short-circuits on ConfigExistsError (exit 2) before reaching the install step at all — side-effect-free. Relaxed the fictional `exits 2 with missing-config` premise (a fresh home never hit that path; the test only passed before because install succeeded against the real fs). Verified the full CLI suite no longer changes ~/.codex/hooks.json (hash + backup-count unchanged across a run). Then repaired the live ~/.codex/hooks.json and codogotchi.toml back to the real home. Other setup-dispatching tests (rpg, setup) were already safe because they inject a fake installHooks via DI.
defect_class: NEW: test escapes sandbox and mutates real user dotfiles
prompt_lesson: State sandboxing (CODOGOTCHI_HOME) and config-target sandboxing (CODOGOTCHI_USER_ROOT) are two independent isolation boundaries; a test that overrides only one can let a real install routine write the developer's actual ~/.codex/~/.cursor. Any test that dispatches a command capable of filesystem installs must either inject a fake installer (DI, as rpg/setup tests do) or sandbox EVERY root the install resolves. A reachability test should never reach a destructive side effect — seed state so it short-circuits. Bonus systemic lesson: when an agent platform (codex-cli) is used as the review subagent and that review runs the test suite, a sandbox-escaping test can sabotage that very platform's integration, masquerading as a platform bug.
test_reachability: Good and now self-guarding. The fix is verified by asserting the real ~/.codex/hooks.json hash and backup count are unchanged after a full `bun test packages/cli` run. A stricter future guard could make the installer refuse to write IDE configs when CODOGOTCHI_HOME points under a /tmp sandbox, as defense-in-depth.

commit: fac4ec0 fix(soa-gate): shorten gate animation TTL from 3min to 30s
problem: The SoA direct-gate sidecar (.son-of-anton/tools/delivery/codogotchi-gate.ts) wrote gate.json with a flat 3-minute TTL (GATE_TTL_MS = 180_000). The renderer uses expires_at to time-box the gate floor animation. Once the persistent floating UI gate badges shipped (phase 08), the long animation TTL became redundant: the badges already tell the user which gate is active, so holding the gate animation for 3 minutes over-rode normal activity-state animation far longer than needed and lagged behind the real workflow.
solution: Drop the flat TTL to 30 seconds (GATE_TTL_MS = 30_000) so the gate.json animation only marks the transition briefly while the badge carries the durable 'which gate is active' signal. Updated the p17-01 TTL assertion (180_000 -> 30_000) and the AGENTS.soa.md contract note. CAVEAT recorded for follow-up: this file lives in the vendored .son-of-anton git subtree, so the change is local-only and the next `/soa update` subtree merge from cesarnml/son-of-anton will revert it unless the same change lands upstream. The durable fix is an upstream son-of-anton commit; this consumer-side edit is a stopgap.
prompt_lesson: When a new always-on UI affordance (the gate badges) supersedes a transient signal (the timed gate animation), revisit the older signal's tuning — it was sized for a world where it was the ONLY indicator. A second, process lesson: behavior constants that live in a vendored subtree need their durable home identified at change time, or the fix silently regresses on the next vendor sync.
test_reachability: Good. p17-01.test.ts pins the exact TTL delta (expires_at - since === 30_000) and passes. Note the subtree's own test suite is NOT part of codogotchi's `bun run test` (which is `bun test packages convex`), so this assertion only runs when the subtree tests are invoked directly or upstream.

commit: 52d156c feat(menubar): add animation badge on floating pet
problem: The floating pet showed gate UI badges (which SoA gate is active) but had no always-on indicator of the underlying activity-state animation the pet was currently playing. A user watching the pet could not read at a glance whether it was Coding, Testing, Thinking, etc. — the animation itself was the only signal, which is ambiguous across visually similar states.
solution: Added a persistent animation badge in the same spirit as the gate badges. Anchored bottom-left INSIDE the floating pet frame (bottom and left edges sit one inset inside the border, contrasting the gate badge which sits above the top border), and scales with the pet frame by reusing GateBadgeLayout.metrics as the single scaling source of truth. The badge is driven by FloatingPetPanelController.apply(state:) so it tracks the live animation, is shown whenever the pet is visible, and re-anchors on every drag/resize tick alongside the existing chrome. Added ActivityState.displayLabel with concise human-readable copy for all 19 states; the four review-family gate states are deliberately disambiguated (Adv Review / Polling / Recording / Review Clean) since their raw names are confusable. The badge panel ignores mouse events and anchors bottom-left, so it never collides with the bottom-right resize affordance or intercepts drags.
prompt_lesson: When a surface already carries one machine-readable signal as chrome (gate badges) but the primary signal (the animation) is only legible to someone who already knows the sprite vocabulary, a human-readable label closes the gap cheaply. Design choice worth stating explicitly in the spec: where multiple chrome elements attach to the same resizable frame, assign each a distinct corner/edge so anchoring rules never fight (gate badge = top-outside, attention bubble = below, animation badge = bottom-left-inside, resize affordance = bottom-right-inside).
test_reachability: Good. AnimationBadgeLayout.frame anchoring (bottom-left inside) and visible-frame clamping are unit-tested; metrics scaling is asserted to share the gate badge source of truth; ActivityState.displayLabel is tested for non-empty, concise (<=14 chars), and unique labels across all 19 cases. Final aesthetics (exact inset feel, legibility over the sprite) still benefit from a visual spot-check.
